facts.statement: The genus was named in 1994 by Eberhard Frey and David Martill to honor Arthur Conan Doyle, the author of The Lost World.
facts.quote: In 1994 it was named by Eberhard Frey and David Martill in honor of Arthur Conan Doyle, who featured large reptilian pterosaurs in his novel The Lost World

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, cataloged as SMNK 1133 PAL, is a reasonably complete skeleton missing the skull, neck, sternum, and some tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The holotype is SMNK 1133 PAL, a reasonably complete skeleton, lacking only a skull, neck, sternum and some caudal vertebrae

facts.statement: Arthurdactylus possessed relatively long wings and exceptionally long wing fingers compared to its 22-centimeter torso, possibly more so than any other pterodactyloid.
facts.quote: Arthurdactylus had, compared to the torso length of 22 centimetres, relatively long wings and especially long wing fingers, perhaps much more so than any other pterodactyloid

facts.statement: The hind limbs of Arthurdactylus were weakly developed.
facts.quote: The hind limbs are however, weakly developed

facts.statement: Arthurdactylus lived during the Early Cretaceous in the Crato Formation of northeastern Brazil.
facts.quote: Arthurdactylus is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous Crato Formation of northeastern Brazil

facts.statement: Arthurdactylus lived between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (119.57 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The original describers classified Arthurdactylus within the family Ornithocheiridae.
facts.quote: The describers assigned Arthurdactylus to the Ornithocheiridae

facts.statement: Paleontologist Alexander Kellner suggests that Arthurdactylus is more closely related to the Anhangueridae, differing from the original classification.
facts.quote: According to Brazilian paleontologist Alexander Kellner, who uses this concept in a different sense, Arthurdactylus can be best indicated as closely related to the Anhangueridae

facts.statement: Arthurdactylus was a medium-sized pterosaur with a wingspan of 4.5 to 4.6 meters and a body mass of 15 kilograms.
facts.quote: It was a medium-sized pterosaur, with a wingspan of 4.5 - 4.6 m and body mass of 15 kg

facts.statement: The authors initially spelled the species name with a hyphenated diacritic that was later corrected to conandoylei in 1998.
facts.quote: They first spelled the species name as Arthurdactylus conan-doylei, thus with a forbidden diacritic sign, and themselves carried out the necessary emendation to conandoylei in 1998
